content: Nitrofurantoin is indicated for the treatment of urinary tract infections (UTIs) caused by susceptible bacteria, including Escherichia coli, Enterococcus species, Enterobacter species, Klebsiella species, Staphylococcus aureus, and Staphylococcus saprophyticus. The dosing regimens vary based on the formulation: 1. Macrocrystals (e.g., Macrodantin, Furadantin suspension, and equivalents): Administer 50-100 mg orally every 6 hours for 7 days or for 3 days after obtaining sterile urine. 2. Monohydrate/Macrocrystals (e.g., Macrobid and equivalents): Administer 100 mg orally every 12 hours for 7 days or for 3 days after obtaining sterile urine. 3. Long-term prophylaxis or suppression: Administer 50-100 mg of macrocrystals orally at bedtime for up to 12 months. Limitations of use: Nitrofurantoin is not indicated for the treatment of pyelonephritis or perinephric abscesses. It is approved for use in patients aged ≥1 month for UTIs caused by susceptible bacteria. Drug Interactions: 1. BCG Vaccine (Live): Nitrofurantoin decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. It is contraindicated. Live bacterial vaccines should be administered only after completing antibiotic therapy. 2. Cholera Vaccine (Live): Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may inactivate the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 3. Darolutamide: Increases nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP). Avoid coadministration or monitor closely for adverse reactions. Dose reduction of BCRP substrate drugs may be necessary. 4. Enasidenib: Increases nitrofurantoin levels by affecting OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. Avoid coadministration or reduce the substrate dosage as per prescribing information. 5. Lasmiditan: Inhibits BCRP in vitro, increasing nitrofurantoin levels. Avoid coadministration or monitor closely. 6. Leniolisib: A BCRP inhibitor that may increase systemic exposure to nitrofurantoin. Avoid coadministration or monitor closely. 7. Microbiota (Oral): Nitrofurantoin decreases the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores. Complete antibiotic regimens 2-4 days before initiating microbiota therapy. 8. Pexidartinib: Increases toxicity risk due to hepatotoxicity. Avoid coadministration with other hepatotoxic agents. 9. Pretomanid: Associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents during therapy. 10. Selinexor: May cause neurological toxicities. Avoid coadministration with medications that cause dizziness or confusion. 11. Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Nitrofurantoin decreases the effects of the vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Contraindicated. Administer live bacterial vaccines only after completing antibiotic therapy. 12. Acalabrutinib: May increase nitrofurantoin exposure by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Use caution and monitor. 13. Aluminum Hydroxide: Decreases nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. 14. Apalutamide: Decreases nitrofurantoin levels by increasing elimination. Monitor closely. 15. Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Nitrofurantoin alters intestinal flora, potentially reducing efficacy. Low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitor closely. 16. Bupivacaine Implant: May increase the risk of methemoglobinemia when coadministered with nitrofurantoin. Monitor closely. 17. Calcium Carbonate: Decreases nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. 18. Conjugated Estrogens (Synthetic): Nitrofurantoin alters intestinal flora, potentially reducing efficacy. Low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitor closely. 19. Danicopan: Increases nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting BCRP. Dose adjustment may be necessary. 20. Dapsone (Topical): Nitrofurantoin may induce methemoglobinemia. Monitor closely. 21. Didanosine: Increases nitrofurantoin levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer nitrofurantoin 2 hours before or several hours after didanosine. 22. Digoxin: Nitrofurantoin alters intestinal flora, potentially increasing digoxin levels. Monitor closely. 23. Eluxadoline: Increases nitrofurantoin levels by decreasing metabolism. Monitor closely. 24. Estradiol: Nitrofurantoin alters intestinal flora, potentially reducing efficacy. Low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitor closely. 25. Fostemsavir: Inhibits BCRP transporters, increasing nitrofurantoin levels. Avoid coadministration or adjust the dose of BCRP substrates. 26. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Increases nitrofurantoin levels by decreasing metabolism. Monitor closely. 27. Levonorgestrel/Ethinyl Estradiol/Ferrous Bisglycinate: Nitrofurantoin alters intestinal flora, potentially reducing efficacy. Low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitor closely. 28. Mestranol: Nitrofurantoin alters intestinal flora, potentially reducing efficacy. Low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitor closely. 29. Mipomersen: Both drugs may increase hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs). 30. Momelotinib: Increases nitrofurantoin toxicity by plasma protein binding competition. Dose adjustment of BCRP substrates may be necessary. 31. Otesaconazole: Inhibits BCRP, increasing nitrofurantoin levels. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or reduce the dose. 32. Oxybutynin (Topical/Transdermal): Increases nitrofurantoin levels by an unspecified mechanism. Monitor closely. 33. Ponatinib: Increases nitrofurantoin levels. Monitor closely. 34. Regorafenib: Inhibits BCRP, increasing nitrofurantoin levels. Monitor closely and consider dose adjustment. 35. Safinamide: Inhibits intestinal BCRP, increasing nitrofurantoin levels. Monitor for adverse effects. 36. Sodium Bicarbonate: Decreases nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. 37. Sodium Citrate/Citric Acid: Decreases nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. 38. Sodium Picosulfate/Magnesium Oxide/Anhydrous Citric Acid: Nitrofurantoin decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora. Monitor closely. 39. Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Velpatasvir inhibits BCRP, increasing nitrofurantoin levels. Monitor closely. 40. Stiripentol: Inhibits BCRP, increasing nitrofurantoin levels. Consider dose reduction of BCRP substrates if adverse effects occur. 41. Tafamidis/Tafamidis Meglumine: Inhibits BCRP, increasing nitrofurantoin levels. Dose adjustment of BCRP substrates may be necessary. 42. Tetracaine: Monitor for signs of methemoglobinemia when coadministered with nitrofurantoin. 43. Trimagnesium Citrate Anhydrous: Decreases nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer nitrofurantoin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium. 44. Vadadustat: Increases nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting BCRP. Monitor for adverse effects and adjust the dose of BCRP substrates as needed. 45. Valoctocogene Roxaparvovec: May increase the risk of hepatotoxicity when combined with nitrofurantoin. Monitor liver enzymes closely. 46. Balsalazide: Nitrofurantoin alters intestinal flora, potentially reducing efficacy. Significance unknown. 47. Biotin: Nitrofurantoin alters intestinal flora, potentially reducing efficacy. Significance unknown. 48. Pantothenic Acid: Nitrofurantoin alters intestinal flora, potentially reducing efficacy. Significance unknown. 49. Pyridoxine: Nitrofurantoin alters intestinal flora, potentially reducing efficacy. Significance unknown.
